items.PAYLOAD: Figures directory contains conceptual diagrams for reality feedback, residual detection, attribution, authority dynamics, representation change, and experimental validation.
Figures are explicitly conceptual rather than implementation diagrams; current forms are Markdown with future publication/architecture formats only proposed.
Figure index describes the adaptive loop, authority cycle, and Theory->Adaptive Authority Dynamics->RAHU research stack as conceptual relations.
Conceptual arrows do not establish implemented data flow, causal identification, or Cerebro topology.
Conceptual loop: Environment->Empirical Outcome->Residual->Attribution->Authority Modification->lower correction or representation expansion->Updated Mechanisms->Future Behavior->Environment.
Defining conceptual pathway is Reality->Residual->Internal Change.
Contradiction should modify future-generating mechanisms and the conceptual correction path distinguishes lower-level correction from representation expansion.
Executable interfaces, timing, measurements, and branch conditions are unspecified.
Authority cycle conceptually links mechanism distribution, behavior, environment, residual, attribution, decay/viability branches, updated authority map, and new mechanism distribution.
Authority is depicted as a dynamic resource whose causal influence varies with empirical performance rather than binary retention/deletion.
Cycle represents the proposed internal selection process, with contradiction-linked attenuation and viability-linked restoration feeding an updated authority map.
Diagram does not establish measured authority, attribution accuracy, or a validated restoration rule.
Source asserts Theory of Adaptive Epistemic Systems->Adaptive Authority Dynamics->RAHU Benchmark, with RAHU intended to test the proposed dynamics.
Theory is labeled the property layer and Adaptive Authority Dynamics the 'law' layer defining time-varying causal influence; label carries source standing only.
Research flow is Theory question->dynamics/law question->benchmark comparative test question.
The 'law' label is not empirical validation, and the benchmark layer does not establish endpoint identity, implementation, execution, or results.
